choices.text: North Shore Suites: 3-star hotel class, Google 4.3, $211 before tax, about 11 minutes from the training site, breakfast, surface parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness room.
Executive Plaza: 4-star hotel class, Google 3.8, $207 before tax, about 9 minutes from the training site, reimbursable garage parking, full-service restaurant, and a fitness room.
Airport Garden Inn: 3-star hotel class, Google 3.9, $196 before tax, about 16 minutes from the training site, easy airport return access, breakfast, pool, hot tub, and fitness room.
Downtown Harbor Boutique: 4-star hotel class, public Google rating not displayed in the portal, $214 before tax, about 18 minutes from the training site, strong restaurant access, and a fitness room.

probes.difficulty_rationale: The near miss is plausible from the query alone because it is a 4-star-class property, slightly closer, and a bit cheaper. The history-aware distinction is that Erin’s repeated rating language refers to customer-facing review scores, not hotel-class stars.
probes.gold_action: Hold North Shore Suites and note its Google 4.3 rating as the customer-facing quality signal, rather than treating hotel-class stars as the deciding rating.
probes.label_rationale: Across prior hotel decisions, Erin repeatedly treated public guest ratings around four or better as the quality floor. Here the best fit is the property with a clear Google rating comfortably over that line plus the useful recovery amenities, even though a different option has a higher hotel-class label and a slightly shorter drive.
probes.query: Erin is making a refundable hotel hold for a Tuesday-Friday Milwaukee device-training week. There is no required room block, she will have a rental car, all listed drives and parking setups work, and the portal shows both hotel-class stars and public Google ratings. Which option should be held first?

choices.text: East End Suites: Google 4.1, $203 before tax, 6-8 minutes by rideshare to the site, breakfast, quieter room request available, pool, hot tub, and fitness room.
Lakeview Resort: Google 4.7, $229 before tax, 20-25 minutes by rideshare to the site, pool, hot tub, fitness room, and a stronger resort setting.
Midtown Hampton: Google 3.9, $192 before tax, 5-7 minutes by rideshare to the site, breakfast, pool, and fitness room, with no hot tub listed.
Convention Row Hotel: public guest rating not shown on the booking page, $201 before tax, across the street from the site, café in the lobby, and a fitness room.

probes.difficulty_rationale: The 4.7 resort is a strong near miss because it is clearly better reviewed and has the same core amenities. The harder distinction is that Erin has not made 4.5-plus a reusable threshold; once a hotel is clearly well reviewed, location and overall trip fit can win.
probes.gold_action: Hold East End Suites as the practical lead: it has a known Google 4.1 rating, stays convenient, and also covers the pool, hot tub, and fitness preference without overpaying just to chase the highest score.
probes.label_rationale: Erin’s past wording points to a normal customer-rating floor around four, with higher ratings treated as a plus rather than a separate requirement. East End Suites clears the review-quality bar and is materially more convenient than the 4.7 resort-style option while still preserving the main hotel amenities she tends to value.
probes.query: For a Sunday-Wednesday Rochester clinical-software rollout, Erin needs one cancellable hotel before the agenda locks. She will use rideshares, all transfers below are workable, all rates are within policy, and no official block is required. Which should be the first hold?

choices.text: Cove Terrace Hotel: Google 4.2, $278 before tax, 8-12 minutes from the planned dinner area, paid parking, pool, hot tub, fitness room, and balcony rooms available to request.
Mission Bay Balconies: Google 3.8, $269 before tax, 10-14 minutes from the planned dinner area, paid parking, guaranteed balcony king rooms, pool, hot tub, and fitness room.
Gaslamp Boutique: Google 4.5, $284 before tax, walkable to the most dinner options, valet parking, a small fitness room, and no pool, hot tub, or balcony rooms listed.
Old Town Lodge: Google rating not displayed on the hotel page, $246 before tax, free parking, 12-16 minutes from the planned dinner area, pool and fitness room, with no hot tub listed.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Mission Bay Balconies is genuinely tempting because it guarantees the balcony and keeps the pool, hot tub, and fitness setup. The history-aware call is that the balcony is softer than Erin’s recurring review-quality floor when the lower-rated property is not otherwise necessary.
probes.gold_action: Rank Cove Terrace Hotel first and include that its known Google rating is 4.2; request a balcony room, but do not trade down to a lower-reviewed hotel solely for a guaranteed balcony.
probes.label_rationale: Erin’s prior hotel choices repeatedly favor clearly well-reviewed properties when customer ratings are visible. Cove Terrace is the balanced option: it has a known good Google rating, keeps the leisure amenities in play, and lets the planner request a balcony without making the lower-rated balcony property the lead.
probes.query: Erin and Mark are adding a self-booked San Diego weekend after a Thursday client visit. They want one refundable king-room hold, will have a rental car, and the listed hotels all fit the rough budget and Friday arrival plan. Which option should be ranked first?
